v1.feedback: The scrimshaw-on-tooth concept is genuinely well-executed — whale, ship, and cross-hatch engravings mapped onto a lathe-turned tooth form give it readable silhouette within 2 seconds and the ivory/warm-bone palette is restrained. The 'oompah' surprise lands as a tuba-player engraving on the back plus a brass bell that fades in with pulsing sound-rings, which is a tasteful tonal swerve rather than a garish one. Two things to tighten: the oompah bell and rings animate below the tooth and may clip out of default camera view — pull the camera back slightly or shift the bell emergence so the full surprise is visible without user interaction. The sound-ring torus bursts read as a bit geometric/disconnected from the organic scrimshaw language; consider replacing them with engraved concentric arcs or stippled vibration lines on the tooth surface itself so the surprise stays within the scrimshaw vocabulary rather than breaking into a different visual register.

v2.feedback: The tuba-player engraving and sound-wave arcs are a genuine oompah swerve on the scrimshaw parent — the idea clearly drove the design. Palette is excellent (bone/ivory, restrained). Two problems: the engraved figures are point-traced outlines that likely read as scattered stipple clouds rather than recognizable silhouettes at default zoom — thicken the stroke by tripling point density along each outline segment and add a faint connecting line geometry so the whale/ship/tuba forms pop in under 2 seconds. Second, the slow auto-orbit means the tuba player on the back takes ~15s to appear; add a subtle camera nudge or a second camera pass so the surprise lands faster.
